chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Hafs al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Instruct the midwife or someone who is next to her that the Prayer be established in its (new-born's) right ear, so it would not be touched by insanity, nor by a following eye, ever.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of reciting Prayer in the newborn's right ear according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the spiritual safeguarding of the newborn through the recitation of Salat (often interpreted as the Adhan or specific supplications) in the right ear, a practice rooted in the belief that the right side is the seat of spiritual receptivity. This ritual serves as an initial invocation of divine protection, shielding the infant from 'lammam' (sudden madness or loss of reason) and 'tabi'ah' (a lingering evil influence or the evil eye), thereby establishing a foundation of faith and health from birth.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban, from Hafs Al Kunasy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Instruct the midwife or someone who is next that the Prayer be established in its (new-born)’s right ear, so it would not be touched by insanity, nor by a following eye, ever’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Aban from Hafs al-Kunasiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Instruct the doctor or someone involved to say Salat (prayer) in the right ear of the child to protect the child against the effect of insanity or the Jinn that follows human beings.’”
